$comment: Radio payload encodings. Shared between the firmware (C++) and the phone
the radio payload verbatim -- so both sides parse exactly these bytes.
Authored by hand from the spec, not generated from either implementation.
A generator would bake one side's bugs into the vectors and the cross-check
would prove nothing. Every vector carries a per-field breakdown so it can be
audited against the spec by reading, without running anything.

groups.layout: lat i32 (deg x 1e7) | lon i32 | alt i16 (m) | hdop u8 | fixAge u8

vectors.name: position_southern_negative
vectors.note: southern and western hemisphere plus altitude below sea level -- three separate sign conversions, which is where a hand-rolled codec goes wrong

vectors.name: position_zero
vectors.note: null island with no fix; the all-zero frame must round-trip like any other

groups.layout: tempC i16 (0.01 C) | humidity u16 (0.01 %) | pressure u32 (Pa) | battery u16 (mV) | uptime u32 (s)

vectors.name: telemetry_typical
vectors.note: 21.35 C, 48.20 %RH, 952.30 hPa, 3.987 V, one day of uptime

vectors.name: telemetry_freezing
vectors.note: -12.75 C exercises the only signed field, and uptime at u32 max exercises the widest one

groups.layout: seq u8 | rssi i16 | snr i8

vectors.name: ack_typical
vectors.note: -97 dBm, +7 dB SNR -- a healthy link at the rendezvous configuration

vectors.name: ack_weak_link
vectors.note: negative SNR below the demodulation floor, and seq at its wrap point. This is the input that drives SF escalation in CLAUDE.md 2.5

groups.layout: UTF-8, max 48 bytes, no null terminator

vectors.name: text_utf8_umlaut
vectors.note: 14 characters but 16 bytes -- the limit in CLAUDE.md 2.2 is bytes, not characters, and a client that truncates by character will overrun it

vectors.name: text_max_48
vectors.note: exactly at the limit; 49 must be rejected
